author: Dalilah James
title: Local groups step up to provide free Thanksgiving meals as demand rises - NewsBreak
text:
By Dalilah James ,
1 hours ago
GEORGETOWN, S.C. (WCBD)— As more families feel the impact of the nation’s longest government shutdown, local organizations and small businesses across Georgetown County are stepping up to make sure no one goes without a Thanksgiving meal.
Helping Hands Food Pantry and Aunny’s Country Kitchen say this year’s effort is fueled almost entirely by community support.
“The people of the community are what makes it possible… it was my vision, but it’s them who makes this a reality,” said Andrea Johnson, Owner of Aunny’s Country Kitchen.
At Aunny’s Country Kitchen, Andrea Johnson is preparing for her 17th annual free Thanksgiving meal a tradition that now relies on dozens of volunteers and donors.
“This feast has gotten bigger than me… there’s no way I could do it on my own,” Johnson said. “Kudos to everybody who supports and donates.”
Helping Hands of Georgetown is also seeing record generosity. The food pantry received so many donations they brought in a storage pod something they haven’t needed in more than 20 years.
“You cannot believe the outpouring… food donations and monetary support,” said Brendon Barber, Executive Director of Helping Hand of Georgetown County.
Helping Hands is distributing Thanksgiving bags while Aunny’s will handle the hot meals cooked, packaged, and ready for anyone who needs one.
“I want everyone to know they’re not alone… there are still people in our community who care,” said Andrea Johnson.
Aunny’s Country Kitchen will offer free meals Thanksgiving Day starting at 11 a.m. and serving until the food runs out. Everyone is welcome and it’s free to the public.
